source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 1 (Constitution: Why and How?).

sections.heading: 1. What is a Constitution?
points: A **constitution** = the **fundamental/supreme law** of a country that lays down how the government is to be constituted, its powers and limits, and the rights of citizens.

sub: Provides a set of **basic rules** for coordination in society.
Specifies **who has power** to make decisions and how government is constituted.
Sets **limits on government power** (protects citizens' rights).
Enables the government to fulfil **aspirations** and create a just society.
Expresses the **fundamental identity** of a people.

sections.heading: 2. Making of the Indian Constitution
points: The **Constituent Assembly** (formed 1946) drafted the Constitution; it met from **December 1946** and worked for ~**2 years, 11 months, 18 days**.
**Dr B.R. Ambedkar** chaired the **Drafting Committee**; **Dr Rajendra Prasad** was the President of the Assembly.
The Constitution was **adopted on 26 November 1949** and came into force on **26 January 1950**.
It drew on Indian experience and borrowed features from other constitutions (British, US, Irish, etc.).

sections.heading: 3. Why the Constitution is Accepted / Authority
points: It was made by a body with **representative credentials** (broadly represented society) and through **deliberation and consensus** (not mere majority).
It **balances flexibility and rigidity** — can be amended but core is protected.
It embodies moral commitments (justice, liberty, equality, fraternity — the **Preamble**).

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Constitution = supreme law; limits government + guarantees rights.
Constituent Assembly drafted it; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.
Adopted 26 Nov 1949; came into force 26 Jan 1950 (Republic Day).
Took ~2 years, 11 months, 18 days; Rajendra Prasad = Assembly President.
Preamble values: justice, liberty, equality, fraternity.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The Constitution was **adopted on 26 Nov 1949** but **came into force 26 Jan 1950**.
**Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee**; **Rajendra Prasad** presided over the Assembly.
A constitution both **empowers and LIMITS** the government.
The **Constituent Assembly** (not Parliament) framed the Constitution.
